newsitem.title: UK: Italian bonds lead field in latest week -Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Italian bonds lead field in latest week -Salomon.

text.p: Italian bonds were the strongest performers in the last week, according to latest data from Salomon Brothers on Friday.

Most of the 17 markets in Salomon Brothers' World Government Bond Index (WGBI) recorded local currency gains in the week to July 24. The index rose by 0.34 percent in local currency terms, but fell by 0.37 percent in dollar terms.
Italian bonds, or BTPs, bounced by 0.81 percent in lira on convergence trades ahead of European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Australian bonds were the second best performers, rising by 0.65 percent in Australian dollars, as the market awaits further easing in monetary policy.
Japanese government bonds (JGBs) gained 0.40 percent in yen. The market benefited from a central bank report showing a weak outlook for the economy.
French bonds rose 0.32 percent in francs, while British gilts were 0.56 percent higher in pounds.

Swiss and German bonds were the only losers on the week in local currencies, with weaker currencies weighing on those markets. Swiss government bonds dipped 0.02 percent in francs, and Bunds dropped 0.06 percent in marks.
The weakness of the mark translated that loss for Bunds into a 2.16 percent fall in dollar terms.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
